text: Joints form the connecting points between pieces of wood used in carpentry and are essential to ensure a strong and stable structure. Common carpentry joints include the square, round, and angle. The square joint is formed by intersecting pieces at right angles, while the round joint, often seen in round bases, features a single straight line of equal length across two pieces. The angle joint, commonly used in corner constructions, involves bevelled edges to create a secure and aesthetically pleasing connection. Each joint requires careful alignment and attention to detail to prevent warping, rotting, and structural weakness. After cutting the wood pieces and assembling the joints, varnish is applied to protect the wood finish and enhance the overall appearance of the finished project.
